children: Copper rises in early Asian trade, as supply shortages and tariff fears continue to drive sentiment. "The market remains on tenterhooks as it awaits the Trump administration's decision on applying a 15% tariff on imports of refined metal," ANZ analysts say in a research note. Supply constraints are also propping up prices, as inventories at Shanghai Futures Exchange warehouses have fallen to their lowest level since 2024, the analysts note. Benchmark three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange are last 0.1% higher at $14,775.00 a ton. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
